problem: The reasoning behavior of large language models remains poorly understood, making it hard to develop and deploy them safely.
approach: Introduce landscape of thoughts (LoT), a visualization tool that represents reasoning trajectories by embedding textual states as numerical features quantifying distance to answer choices, then visualizing them in 2D using t-SNE.
contribution: LoT effectively distinguishes strong from weak models, correct from incorrect answers, uncovers undesirable reasoning patterns like low consistency, and enables lightweight verifiers that boost reasoning accuracy and test-time scaling.

problem: Multilayer perceptrons encode information both in weights and in training dynamics, but current analysis focuses on single checkpoints rather than temporal evolution.
approach: Construct temporal parameter-graphs across training snapshots and embed them in hyperbolic space (Poincaré ball) using a meta-learning framework that maintains equivariance to neuron permutations.
contribution: Hyperbolic temporal representations expose how structure emerges during training, offering intrinsic geometric explanations of self-organization in neural networks.

problem: Existing benchmarks only evaluate LLMs on isolated function-level code generation, not on building entire software systems that require orchestrating components, maintaining state consistency, and managing lifecycle constraints.
approach: Propose a benchmark of 101 real-world Android app development problems where LLMs must implement full apps from natural language specs; use a multi-agent system to generate test cases and automated evaluation framework.
contribution: First benchmark for end-to-end app development that evaluates whether LLMs can construct complete software systems with context-aware, robust code; enables reproducible assessment without human intervention.

problem: Identifying the most suitable pre-trained model for a time series task by individually fine-tuning each candidate is time-consuming.
approach: SwiftTS uses a learning-guided dual-encoder architecture that embeds time series and candidate models, computes patchwise compatibility scores, and employs a horizon-adaptive expert composition module to predict which pre-trained model fits best.
contribution: SwiftTS achieves state-of-the-art performance in time series pre-trained model selection across 14 downstream datasets and 8 pre-trained models.

problem: Existing attribution methods for LLMs rely on linear approximations and encoder-based designs that fail to capture the causal and semantic complexities of autoregressive generation in decoder-only models.
approach: Propose HETA, which combines semantic transition vectors, Hessian-based sensitivity scores, and KL divergence to measure information loss when tokens are masked, producing context-aware and causally faithful attributions.
contribution: HETA establishes a new standard for interpretability in autoregressive language models, outperforming existing methods in attribution faithfulness and alignment with human annotations.

problem: Diffusion Large Language Models face a severe quality-speed trade-off where faster parallel decoding leads to significant performance degradation due to irreversibility and early error context accumulation.
approach: Introduce WINO, a training-free decoding algorithm that uses a parallel draft-and-verify mechanism to aggressively draft multiple tokens while using bidirectional context to verify and re-mask suspicious ones for refinement.
contribution: WINO improves the quality-speed trade-off in DLLMs: on GSM8K it accelerates inference by 6× while improving accuracy by 2.58%; on Flickr30K captioning it achieves 10× speedup with higher performance.

problem: The memory consumption of QKV linear projections in multi-head attention is often overlooked despite being a significant bottleneck in LLM training.
approach: Propose Point-Approximate Matrix Multiplication (PAMM), a tensor compression technique that reduces memory of QKV projections by up to 512× through approximation while maintaining comparable perplexity.
contribution: PAMM effectively erases the memory footprint of QKV projections and is fully composable with efficient attention techniques like FlashAttention.

problem: Forecasting evolution of 3D medical scans requires handling irregular temporal sampling and voxel-level predictions, tasks not well addressed by existing models that rely on fixed grid times or single prior scans.
approach: CRONOS learns a spatio-temporal velocity field that transports context volumes toward a target volume at arbitrary times, operating directly in 3D voxel space and supporting both discrete and continuous timestamps.
contribution: CRONOS is the first to achieve continuous sequence-to-image forecasting for 3D medical data, outperforming baselines across Cine-MRI, perfusion CT, and longitudinal MRI datasets.

problem: Modern neural networks exhibit low-loss connectivity between basins yet remain confined to single basins during optimization, a paradox not fully explained by energetic barriers.
approach: Identify entropic barriers arising from curvature variations along connectivity paths; show curvature systematically rises away from minima, producing effective forces that bias noisy dynamics back toward endpoints.
contribution: Reveals that curvature-induced entropic forces, not just energetic barriers, govern connectivity and confinement in deep learning loss landscapes, shaping late-time solution localization.

problem: Sewing pattern creation traditionally relies on skilled artisans' intuition, and existing generative approaches either act as data replicators without understanding garment construction or struggle with low-level coordinate regression.
approach: GarmentGPT tokenizes continuous pattern curves into discrete codebook indices using RVQ-VAE, then uses a fine-tuned Vision-Language Model to autoregressively predict discrete token sequences for compositional reasoning.
contribution: First framework for latent space generation of sewing patterns achieving 95.62% panel accuracy and 81.84% stitch accuracy on structured datasets, significantly outperforming existing methods.

problem: Post-training quantization of billion-scale 3D reconstruction transformers faces unique obstacles: data-independent special tokens induce heavy-tailed activation distributions and multi-view calibration is unstable.
approach: QuantVGGT introduces dual-smoothed fine-grained quantization with Hadamard rotation and channel smoothing, plus noise-filtered diverse sampling that filters outliers and constructs frame-aware calibration clusters.
contribution: Achieves 3.7× memory reduction and 2.5× acceleration in real hardware inference while preserving over 98% reconstruction quality.

problem: DNA foundation models often lag behind task-specific methods for unclear reasons, and existing approaches don't fully leverage structural information in large-scale protein datasets.
approach: AntigenLM pretrains a generative DNA language model on influenza genomes with intact, aligned functional units to capture evolutionary constraints, then fine-tunes on time-series hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences.
contribution: AntigenLM accurately forecasts future antigenic variants across regions and subtypes while outperforming phylogenetic models, demonstrating that preserving genomic structure is critical for DNA language models.

problem: Hallucination detection methods achieve strong performance within a single domain but suffer from poor cross-domain generalization.
approach: Observe that hallucination-initiated multi-turn dialogues universally exhibit larger uncertainty fluctuations than factual ones; propose SpikeScore which quantifies abrupt fluctuations in uncertainty across turns.
contribution: SpikeScore achieves strong cross-domain separability between hallucinated and non-hallucinated responses, outperforming baselines and generalization-oriented methods.

problem: Task and motion planning relies heavily on manually engineered planning domains, limiting long-horizon planning reliability and automation.
approach: PDDLLM automatically induces symbolic predicates and actions from demonstration trajectories by combining LLM reasoning with physical simulation roll-outs, requiring minimal manual domain initialization.
contribution: Across 1,200 tasks in nine environments, PDDLLM achieves at least 20% higher success rates than LLM-based planning baselines with reduced token costs and successful deployment on physical robots.

problem: It is unclear which properties of synthetic data affect generalization error beyond heuristic principles like 'data should be close to the target distribution'.
approach: Theoretically analyze high-dimensional regression to show that covariance shift between target and synthetic distributions affects generalization, while mean shift surprisingly does not.
contribution: Covariance matching is optimal in some regimes; the theoretical insights for linear models carry over to deep neural networks, and covariance matching outperforms recent synthetic data selection approaches.

problem: Existing on-the-fly category discovery methods rely on hash-based encodings that overestimate the number of categories and suffer from hash function sensitivity.
approach: Reformulate OCD into open-set recognition and fully novel OCD; employ soft class thresholding for known classes and Adaptive Gaussian Expansion to dynamically model probability density functions for novel categories.
contribution: AGE achieves state-of-the-art performance in on-the-fly category discovery across multiple datasets with significantly improved real-time classification feasibility.

problem: Recent embedding models focus on data scaling or synthesis while neglecting systematic exploration of training techniques and data quality improvements.
approach: KaLM-Embedding-V2 implements a 0.5B model with bidirectional attention and proposes a progressive multi-stage training pipeline combining pre-training, fine-tuning, and contrastive distillation with focal reweighting and hard-negative mining.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, rivaling models 3-26× larger while being compact.

problem: Evaluating LLM-based agentic systems acting as co-scientists requires realistic end-to-end research scenarios integrating data analysis, interpretation, and new insights from experimental data.
approach: HeurekaBench creates benchmarks with exploratory, open-ended research questions grounded in scientific studies; uses a semi-automated pipeline with multiple LLMs to extract insights and verify against reported findings.
contribution: Enables quantitative end-to-end evaluation of scientific agents; shows adding a critic module improves ill-formed responses by up to 22%, setting a path toward rigorous agentic system evaluation.

problem: In-context learning under complex non-i.i.d. scenarios lacks theoretical understanding of which factors ensure generalization.
approach: Establish stability bounds for transformers trained with mini-batch gradient descent and introduce a distribution-level discrepancy measure; derive a generalization error bound for ICL with asymptotic convergence.
contribution: Reveals that token-wise prediction errors accumulate over time and can cause generalization collapse if length is unconstrained; provides theoretical guarantees for ICL generalization.

problem: Despite strong performance of test-time scaling methods like OpenAI's o1, the conditions in training data under which long chains-of-thought emerge and improve performance remain unclear.
approach: Study test-time scaling for transformers on an in-context weight prediction task for linear regression; analyze relationships between test-time compute, context length, and task difficulty.
contribution: Characterizes task hardness via the smallest eigenvalue of feature covariance; shows training on diverse, relevant, and hard tasks results in best test-time scaling performance.

problem: Existing learning-based feature upsamplers require re-training for every feature extractor and do not generalize to different feature types at inference time.
approach: AnyUp proposes an inference-time feature-agnostic upsampling architecture that can be applied to any vision feature at any resolution without encoder-specific training.
contribution: Sets state-of-the-art upsampling performance, generalizes to different feature types, preserves feature semantics while being efficient for diverse downstream tasks.

problem: Existing protein generation models underutilize vast structural information in large-scale protein datasets; the challenge is how to exploit abundant unlabeled protein data using unsupervised pretraining.
approach: RigidSSL introduces rigidity-based pretraining using inertial frame canonicalization, combines large-scale perturbations with molecular dynamics views, and applies rigid-body flow matching with Invariant Point Attention.
contribution: RigidSSL learns stable, geometry-aware representations that improve downstream protein generation by better exploiting low-cost unlabeled protein datasets.

problem: Multi-objective flexible job shop scheduling problems remain underexplored in neural combinatorial optimization, limiting applicability in practical multi-criteria decision-making scenarios.
approach: Propose a decomposition-based NCO method with DCAN, a dual conditional attention network that takes objective preferences and learns adaptable policies; decompose MOFJSPs into subproblems with different preferences.
contribution: Outperforms traditional multi-objective optimization methods and generalizes well across diverse problem instances, enabling multi-criteria scheduling via neural methods.

problem: RL training of LLMs stalls on hard problems where the policy cannot generate rollouts with non-zero rewards, requiring better credit assignment.
approach: Interventional Training leverages single-step oracle interventions to provide language feedback on intermediate reasoning steps; patches the model via supervised fine-tuning on the on-policy rollout plus correction.
contribution: With approximately 100 oracle interventions, InT solves 16% more hard test problems previously unsolved and improves performance across multiple standard evaluations.

problem: Search agents trained via RL are limited by shallow tool-use depth and error accumulation over multiple iterative interactions.
approach: WebSeer introduces a self-reflection mechanism within RL training, constructs a large dataset annotated with reflection patterns, and uses a two-stage training framework unifying cold start and RL.
contribution: Using a single 14B model, achieves state-of-the-art results on HotpotQA (72.3% accuracy) and SimpleQA (90.0% accuracy) with strong generalization to out-of-distribution datasets.

problem: Conventional image codecs optimized for human vision are ill-suited for MLLMs, which have diverse downstream tasks with varying feature-level dependencies.
approach: CoTAM adaptively protects multi-level features by using CLIP's shallow-layer attention to generate importance maps; the decoder integrates a lightweight adapter with multi-level loss to preserve both low-level details and high-level semantics.
contribution: Achieves up to 35.99% bitrate saving while maintaining MLLM task performance, outperforming previous neural codecs.

problem: Research on state space models like Mamba for time series classification has remained limited, with insufficient benchmarking and reproducibility.
approach: MambaSL minimally redesigns the selective SSM and projection layers of a single-layer Mamba guided by four TSC-specific hypotheses; re-evaluates 20 baselines across all 30 UEA datasets under a unified protocol.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on the UEA benchmark among 21 models with statistically significant improvements and reproducible public checkpoints.

problem: Applying diffusion models to CT reconstruction is challenging due to correlated noise, artifact structures, system geometry dependence, and misaligned value ranges not typical of natural image generation.
approach: DM4CT benchmarks nine diffusion-based methods alongside seven baselines including model-based and unsupervised approaches across medical and industrial CT datasets with sparse-view and noisy configurations.
contribution: Provides detailed insights into diffusion model behavior for CT reconstruction; a public real-world high-resolution synchrotron dataset enables rigorous evaluation.

problem: Prompt optimization methods target point-wise accuracy but do not enforce paraphrase invariance or searching stability, leaving LLMs brittle to small semantic-preserving paraphrases.
approach: TARE introduces textual sharpness as a formal criterion for robustness in the semantic space of prompts; alternates between an inner adversarial search stressing prompts with hard paraphrases and an outer robust selection.
contribution: Generates prompts that preserve accuracy under paraphrasing; ATARE adapts with anisotropic weights and balances exploration-fidelity, outperforming accuracy-only prompt search.

problem: Classical influence functions face challenges when applied to deep neural networks due to non-invertible Hessians and high-dimensional parameter spaces.
approach: Propose Bayesian influence functions that replace Hessian inversion with loss landscape statistics estimated via stochastic-gradient MCMC sampling, capturing higher-order parameter interactions.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on predicting retraining experiments while scaling efficiently to billion-parameter neural networks.

problem: Extending PPO to expressive, high-capacity policy models like continuous normalizing flows is challenging because likelihood evaluation along the full flow trajectory is computationally expensive and numerically unstable.
approach: PolicyFlow approximates importance ratios using velocity field variations along a simple interpolation path; proposes Brownian Regularizer as an implicit entropy regularizer to prevent mode collapse.
contribution: Integrates expressive CNF policies with PPO-style objectives without requiring full trajectory likelihood evaluation, achieving competitive or superior performance on diverse tasks.

problem: Speech-language models treat speech understanding as a single black box and reason weakly about non-content aspects under sparse supervision.
approach: Adopt a modular perspective using a world model that learns forward dynamics over latent states, factorizing speech understanding into four modules communicating through a causal graph.
contribution: First graph-based modular speech model for explicit reasoning, enabling counterfactual interventions and interpretability; supports causal analysis under partial supervision.

problem: Reward-guided image editing requires preserving semantic content of the source image while enhancing a target reward, a task largely unexplored in diffusion/flow-matching models.
approach: Formulate editing as a trajectory optimal control problem where the reverse process is a controllable trajectory from the source image; iteratively update adjoint states to steer the editing.
contribution: Significantly outperforms inversion-based baselines in balancing reward maximization and fidelity to the source image without reward hacking.

problem: Existing inductive link prediction methods for knowledge hypergraphs assume fixed relational vocabulary and cannot generalize to novel relation types or novel entities.
approach: Propose HYPER as a foundation model that learns and transfers across different relation types of varying arities by encoding entities along with their positions in hyperedges.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods in both node-only and node-and-relation inductive settings, showing strong generalization to unseen higher-arity relational structures.

problem: While activation steering reduces hallucinations, existing methods require real-time monitoring during inference; models still lack the ability to abstain from answering questions they don't know.
approach: CASAL directly bakes activation steering benefits into model weights via amortized optimization, training only a submodule of a single transformer layer.
contribution: Reduces hallucination by 30-40% across multiple benchmarks with 30× better compute efficiency than LoRA baselines; generalizes to OOD domains and works with both dense and MoE models.

problem: Test-time scaling methods suffer from high inference latency due to synchronization overhead when scaling along parallel and sequential dimensions.
approach: ATTS follows hypothesis testing to enable asynchronous inference through online calibration and proposes an ordinal classification algorithm supporting a three-stage rejection sampling pipeline.
contribution: Delivers up to 56.7× speedup in test-time scaling and 4.14× throughput improvement while maintaining accurate rejection rate control and no accuracy loss.

problem: Sequential quantization frameworks treat all layers equally during post-training quantization, which may be suboptimal when facing challenging bit-width settings.
approach: SliderQuant employs adaptive sliding quantization with inter-layer designs targeting shallow/intermediate/deep layers and intra-layer incremental strategies to reduce quantization error.
contribution: Significantly reduces quantization errors across layers, improving LLM quantization quality at challenging bit-widths.

problem: Monotonicity constraints in value function factorization limit expressiveness and restrict the range of joint action values, hindering optimal policy learning.
approach: POW iteratively identifies potentially optimal joint actions and assigns higher training weights through a theoretically grounded weighted training process.
contribution: Guarantees recovery of the true optimal policy and consistently surpasses state-of-the-art value-based MARL methods across diverse environments.

problem: Graph neural networks overlook multi-way and hierarchical relationships; existing topological deep learning models are restricted to undirected settings and fail to capture directed higher-order patterns.
approach: Introduce Semi-Simplicial Neural Networks operating on semi-simplicial sets that encode directed higher-order motifs; propose Routing-SSNs that dynamically select informative relations.
contribution: Strictly more expressive than standard graph and TDL models; achieves state-of-the-art on brain dynamics classification (27% improvement over second-best) and scales efficiently.

problem: Few-shot anomaly detection is challenging because limited samples make differentiation between normal and abnormal features difficult, especially under category-agnostic conditions.
approach: FoundAD leverages foundation visual encoders to learn a nonlinear projection operator onto the natural image manifold; anomaly amount correlates with embedding differences.
contribution: Supports multi-class detection with competitive performance while surpassing other approaches in model size and inference efficiency.
